title: How I Built My Own AI Grading Tool and You Can Too (No Coding Required)
author: Teaching With Intelligence
summary: Privacy-first AI grading systems are now achievable without third-party platforms or student data exposure. Building a workflow that combines Claude API with Google Drive enables teachers to grade student work while maintaining complete data control. The system eliminates the need for expensive subscription platforms while providing superior grading quality. Teachers configure rubrics in plain language, Claude evaluates work against those standards, and results store locally or in teacher-controlled systems. This approach solves critical education technology problems: cost (free to minimal expense), privacy (no student data leaves the school), integration (works with existing tools like Google Classroom and Drive), and explainability (teachers see exactly why grades were assigned). The implementation involves setting up Claude API access, configuring folder structures for student submissions, creating grading rubrics as plain-text specifications, building an automation sequence that reads submissions and generates feedback, and routing results back to the teacher. Unlike commercial platforms that add a data collection layer, this system keeps teachers in control. The technical barrier is essentially zero with modern automation tools like n8n or Make. The article walks through each step: account setup, folder organization, prompt crafting for rubric conversion, automation design, and integration back to existing classroom systems. This represents a larger pattern of teachers building custom AI tools rather than adopting one-size-fits-all products, regaining agency over their assessment practices while improving grading consistency and quality.
points: Teachers can build privacy-first grading systems without coding or expensive third-party platforms
Claude API integration with Google Drive enables complete data control and local processing
Plain-language rubric conversion eliminates the need for technical specification writing
Automation-first approach reduces teacher burden while improving grading consistency
Custom-built systems outperform commercial off-the-shelf education platforms in flexibility and privacy
quotes: How to build a privacy-first AI grading workflow using Claude and Google Drive—no third-party platforms, no student data leaving your control.
Privacy-first means your student data never leaves your school or teacher account. The grading happens in your systems, with your rules, at your pace.

You do not need to hand your student data to a third-party platform to get AI grading. You can build it yourself. The tool stack costs almost nothing. And your students remain in control of their own data.
The implementation is simpler than most teachers expect. You do not need to write code. You do not need to understand machine learning. You do not need to learn Python.
This is where teachers stop waiting for edtech companies to build the right product and start building it themselves.

A five-step workflow that keeps AI support fast, realistic, and teacher-led is all that is needed to grade more thoughtfully and quickly.” Archived from Teaching With Intelligence on April 19, 2026 by Tim.
